exposure: Cervical venous plexus (CV) volume measured by MRI
Placental location (anterior placenta previa vs. posterior placenta previa)
cohort: 59 patients with placenta accreta spectrum and placenta previa who underwent a cesarean section with prophylactic balloon occlusion of the internal iliac arteries.
finding: In patients with posterior placenta previa, a smaller cervical venous plexus volume significantly correlated with increased intraoperative blood loss, predicting massive hemorrhage (IBL >= 2500 mL).
mod_finding: A smaller cervical venous plexus volume on preoperative MRI predicted a higher intraoperative bleeding risk specifically during cesarean section for placenta accreta spectrum with posterior placenta previa.
